title: Bounded function presentations and compatibility of evaluated cokernels

from.place: Proof, descent through the common-stage colimit: local finite presentation at algebraic-closure coefficients; coefficient matrices and their geometric-fibre rank comparison before the rank-constancy and minor arguments.

statement: Let \(\ell\) be prime, \(X\) a scheme with noetherian underlying space, and \(f:Y\to X\) weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. For a topological space \(T\), let \(F_\ell(T)\) be the ring of continuous functions \(T\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\) whose image is contained in a finite subextension of \(\mathbf Q_\ell\) [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], with pointwise operations. Write \(A_T=p_T^*\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}\) for the condensed coefficient ring object on a scheme \(T\) [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and \(B_X\) for the sheafification of the presheaf \(U\mapsto F_\ell(|U|)\) on the pro-etale site of \(X\) [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume supplied an isomorphism of ring objects \(A_X\simeq B_X\). Let \(P\) be an \(A_X\)-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and suppose that \(f^*P\), over \(A_Y\), is the cokernel of a map \(A_Y^m\to A_Y^n\) for finite ranks. Then there exist a pro-etale cover \(C\) of \(Y\), fixed integers \(n,m\ge0\), and matrices \(M_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(F_\ell(|C_i|))\), with these properties. First, the vector spaces \(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^n/\operatorname{range}(M_i(x))\) and \(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^n/\operatorname{range}(M_j(y))\) are linearly equivalent whenever \((C_i\to Y\to X)(x)=(C_j\to Y\to X)(y)\). Second, for every open subscheme \(V\subseteq C_i\), there is a unital ring homomorphism \(\phi_{i,V}:F_\ell(|V|)\to\operatorname{End}_{A_V}(A_V)\) and an isomorphism of \(A_V\)-module sheaves from \(P|_V\) to the cokernel of the biproduct morphism with entries \(\phi_{i,V}(M_i(k,j)|_V)\). Evaluation in the first clause is ordinary point evaluation followed by the associated linear map. No rank calculation, local constancy or finite freeness is asserted.

proof.text: Unpack the finite presentation on Y. Cover Y by its affine open cover, and each affine by the singleton cover supplied by the affine contractible-extension theorem. Bind the covers without increasing their index universe. The theorem supplies affineness and weak contractibility for the terminal object on each cover scheme's own full small site, by applying its final clause to the identity morphism.

proof.text: Use the constructed coefficient scalar/evaluation datum and its four naturality/basis properties. Pull the fixed presentation to each cover member using the normalized regular-module pullback isomorphism, biproduct comparisons, and preservation of cokernels. Recover the morphism from its biproduct inclusions and projections. Scalar surjectivity chooses one bounded function for each matrix entry. The component-matrix identity proves that these functions reconstruct the pulled-back presentation. All ranks are the original fixed m and n, including zero ranks.

source.place: Section 4, finite-matrix refinement: presentation and geometric-fibre comparison after coefficient realization (steps 1--3)

proof.text: For each open subscheme use its scalar ring map from the same coefficient datum. Pull the reconstructed matrix presentation along the open immersion. The generic free-pullback matrix identity and scalar restriction conjugacy identify its entries with restrictions of the chosen functions. Compose the inverse-image composition isomorphisms and the preserved-cokernel isomorphisms to obtain the required presentation on that open.

source.place: Section 4, finite-matrix refinement: presentation and geometric-fibre comparison after coefficient realization (steps 1--3)

proof.text: Apply the additive finite-colimit-preserving geometric evaluation functor to each reconstructed matrix presentation. The finite-biproduct coordinate equivalence sends the evaluated morphism to the ordinary value matrix, by evaluating each scalar entry on one. The cokernel has dimension n minus matrix rank, by the linear cokernel/range quotient isomorphism and rank-nullity. At two points with the same image in X the natural comparison of evaluated pullback functors gives equal dimensions. Each quotient of the finite-dimensional coordinate space is finite-dimensional, so equality of dimensions gives the required linear equivalence. These calculations prove only fibre compatibility, not any rank local constancy or freeness assertion.

theorem exists_condensedQbar_compatible_function_presentations
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : WeaklyEtale f)
    (hcoeff : Nonempty
      (Mon.mk (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X) ≅
        Mon.mk (padicAlgClSheaf X ℓ)))
    (P : CategoryTheory.Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X))
    (hP : Mod.IsFinitelyPresented
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) Y)
      ((CondensedRing.upperStar (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) f).obj P)) :
    ∃ (C : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage Y) (n m : ℕ)
      (B : ∀ i : C.I₀,
        Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) (PadicAlgCl.finiteIntermediateFieldValued ℓ (C.X i))),
      (∀ (i j : C.I₀) (x : C.X i) (y : C.X j),
        (C.f i ≫ f) x = (C.f j ≫ f) y →
        Nonempty
          (((Fin n → PadicAlgCl ℓ) ⧸ LinearMap.range
            (((B i).map (condensedQbarFunctionEval x)).toLin')) ≃ₗ[PadicAlgCl ℓ]
            ((Fin n → PadicAlgCl ℓ) ⧸ LinearMap.range
              (((B j).map (condensedQbarFunctionEval y)).toLin')))) ∧
      ∀ (i : C.I₀) (V : (C.X i).Opens),
        ∃ φ : PadicAlgCl.finiteIntermediateFieldValued ℓ V.toScheme →+*
            End (Mod.regular (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) V.toScheme)),
          Nonempty
            ((CondensedRing.upperStar (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ)
              ((V.ι ≫ C.f i) ≫ f)).obj P ≅
              cokernel (biproduct.matrix fun j k ↦
                φ (condensedQbarFunctionComp V.ι.base.hom (B i k j))))
